unsuccessful_outcome_surface_label: Example State official voter-information unsuccessful-outcome fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes that end in no-match, unable-to-process, rejected, or closed outcomes keep the public meaning of the result and the next authoritative action clear enough that the voter does not have to guess whether to retry, correct something, switch routes, or contact the office.
unsuccessful_outcome_vocabulary_note: The route explains the ordinary public meaning of unsuccessful outcomes such as no matching record, mismatched information, unable to process here, closed window, duplicate/already completed, temporary service issue, or contact office.
retryable_vs_nonretryable_note: The route distinguishes when the voter should correct and retry the same path, when to use a different official route, and when repeated resubmission is not the next safe action.
same_route_correction_note: When the same route remains appropriate, the route identifies what can be corrected or rechecked without forcing blind resubmission.
alternate_route_or_status_note: When the same route is no longer the right lane, the route identifies the authoritative status, correction, or office-help path that should be used next.
reference_or_attempt_note: The route keeps any useful reference number, attempt identifier, or bounded attempt context visible when later help depends on it.
context_preservation_note: The route preserves entered values or other bounded context needed for correction or office help without exposing unnecessary sensitive data.
help_or_escalation_note: The route tells the voter when ordinary office help is the next step and when the problem should be treated as a rights, safety, or wrongful-denial escalation instead.
accessible_unsuccessful_outcome_note: Unsuccessful-outcome language, next steps, and help transitions remain available in accessible text and are reviewable with common assistive technology and mobile constraints.
